s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive pigmented lesion of the lip with local extension
salient_findings: Slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion
Brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion
Multiple pigmented papules with focal ulcerations on the lip
key_facts: 4-year history of the lesion
Initial lesion size: 1 cm × 0.5 cm
Lesion progressively increased in size without symptoms
Brownish discoloration of the skin appeared after 3 years
No significant medical or family history
No smoking or drinking history
Lip was slightly swollen
Intraoral lesion extended from the labial frenum to 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth
Lesion was non-tender, non-indurated, and exhibited focal ulcerations
No cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions found
Normal complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis
Unremarkable chest radiography

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pigmented lesion with local extension and focal ulcerations

shortlist.label: Labial melanotic macule
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion on the lip with brownish discoloration

shortlist.label: Melanocytic nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion with progressive increase in size

shortlist.label: Laugier-Hunziker syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesions on the lip with local extension and brownish discoloration

raw.rationale: The lesion's progressive increase in size over 4 years, the appearance of brownish discoloration, and the presence of focal ulcerations are concerning features for malignancy, particularly in the context of a pigmented lesion.

rejected.label: Labial melanotic macule
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solitary, stable, and asymptomatic pigmented lesion, which does not match the progressive nature of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Melanocytic nevus
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-circumscribed, benign-appearing lesion, which does not explain the ulcerations and progressive growth seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Mucosal melanosis
rejected.why: Refers to benign pigmentation of mucous membranes, which does not account for the invasive and potentially malignant features of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Laugier-Hunziker syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by benign pigmentation of the lips and oral mucosa, often accompanied by longitudinal melanonychia, which does not match the clinical presentation of a progressively enlarging and ulcerating lesion.
